extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners handling biotechnology patent applications involving biological deposits or nucleotide/amino acid sequence disclosures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for (A) biological material deposits referenced in patent applications (when required, how examiners treat missing/insufficient deposits, and what must appear in the specification) and (B) requirements for submitting nucleotide/amino acid sequence listings in XML (WIPO ST.26) for applications filed on/after July 1, 2022.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of Statement of Availability of Deposit (request content)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will certify whether a deposit has been stated to have been made under conditions which make it available to the public as of the issue date of the patent grant, provided the request is made to a Director of Technology Center (TC) 1600 and contains the following information: (A) the name and address of the depository; (B) the accession number given to the deposit; (C) the patent number and issue date of the patent referring to the deposit; and (D) the name and address of the requesting party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persons requesting a certificate should contact the TC 1600 Director's office directly and should not submit a request via the examiner of record. The Office will not certify availability until issuance of a U.S. patent referencing the deposit; requests regarding deposits in applications that have not issued as patents will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duty under 37 CFR 1.809(a): determine need and acceptability of deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner shall determine pursuant to § 1.104 in each application for patent, reissue, or reexamination whether a deposit is needed, and if needed, whether a deposit actually made is acceptable for patent purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a deposit is needed and has not been made or replaced/supplemented according to regulations, the examiner, where appropriate, shall reject the affected claims under the appropriate provision of 35 U.S.C. 112, explaining why a deposit is needed and/or why a deposit actually made cannot be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant/patent owner reply options to deposit-based rejection (37 CFR 1.809(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to a rejection under paragraph (a), an applicant/patent owner must either (1) make an acceptable original, replacement, or supplemental deposit, or assure the Office in writing that an acceptable deposit will be made; or (2) argue why a deposit is not needed or why a deposit actually made should be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other replies are nonresponsive and may result in abandonment. The rejection will be repeated until (b)(1) is satisfied or the examiner is convinced no deposit is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of allowability and three-month deposit period (37 CFR 1.809(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is otherwise in condition for allowance except for a needed deposit and the Office has received a written assurance that an acceptable deposit will be made, the Office may issue a notice of allowability and set a three-month period from the mailing date of the notice within which the deposit must be made to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This three-month period is not extendable under § 1.136. Failure to make the needed deposit in accordance with this requirement will be considered a failure to prosecute under 35 U.S.C. 133 and will result in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification content requirements for deposited biological material (37 CFR 1.809(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each deposit made pursuant to these regulations, the specification shall contain: (1) the accession number for the deposit; (2) the date of the deposit; (3) a description of the deposited biological material sufficient to specifically identify it and to permit examination and verification; and (4) the name and address of the depository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description must permit verification that the deposited biological material is what is disclosed and, once the patent issues, must be sufficient to aid in resolution of infringement questions. The more information provided about the deposited material, the better the examiner will be able to compare identity and characteristics with the prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of amendments adding deposit information (37 CFR 1.809(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment required by paragraphs (d)(1), (d)(2) or (d)(4) (accession number, deposit date, depository name/address) must be filed before or with the payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants need to make necessary deposits well prior to payment of the issue fee so the accession number is received in time to amend the specification as required. Such amendments are filed under 37 CFR 1.312.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden allocation concerning necessity of access to biological material
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office initially bears the burden to establish that access to a biological material is necessary for satisfaction of statutory patentability requirements under 35 U.S.C. 112. Once the Office meets this burden, the burden shifts to the applicant/patent owner to demonstrate that access is not necessary, is already available, or that a deposit will be made in accordance with the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should provide scientific reasoning when concluding that access is necessary (see grounds of rejection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection ground: 35 U.S.C. 112(a) — enablement when deposit needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejection for lack of an enabling disclosure without access to a specific biological material where a person skilled in the art could not make or use the invention as claimed without access to the specific biological material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rejection should be accompanied by evidence of scientific reasoning supporting that conclusion (see MPEP § 2164.06(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection ground: 35 U.S.C. 112(a) — written description when deposit absent
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection for lack of written description may arise where the application as filed does not contain a description to support an amendment to the specification or claims, or where amendment to claims/other application parts is not described in the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such situations may also give rise to objections under 35 U.S.C. 132 (new matter) and a requirement that the amendment be canceled. See MPEP § 2163 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection ground: 35 U.S.C. 112(a) — best mode (rare in ex parte)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection for lack of a best mode requires a finding that at filing the inventor knew of a specific material considered better than others and that the inventor concealed that best mode by failing to adequately describe it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best mode rejections are rare in ex parte examination; see case law (Chemcast) and MPEP § 2165 for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection ground: 35 U.S.C. 112(b) — indefiniteness as applied to deposit issues
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection for indefiniteness may be applied where terms in the claims and/or scope of the invention are unclear because of an incomplete or inaccurate description or absence of reference to a biological material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must provide reasons why claim terms are unclear due to deposit-related disclosure deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection ground: 35 U.S.C. 112(b) — claims must set forth what inventor regards as the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection that claims do not set forth the subject matter that the inventor regards as the invention requires citation of evidence (not in the application as filed) supporting the rejection; disagreements between disclosure and claim scope should be addressed under 112(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite precedents (e.g., In re Prater, In re Ehrreich) when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of deposits made in IDAs under the Budapest Treaty
rubrics_metrics.description: A deposit accepted in any International Depositary Authority (IDA) under the Budapest Treaty shall be accepted for patent purposes if made under conditions which comply with 37 CFR 1.806 and 1.808(a) concerning term of deposit and permissible conditions on access once the patent is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure deposits under Budapest Treaty meet USPTO regulatory requirements on term and access conditions (see MPEP references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies to examiner rejections based on deposit issues — acceptable written assurance standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A written assurance will be accepted if it clearly states that an acceptable deposit will be made within the required time and under conditions which satisfy these rules; if such an acceptable written assurance is made, the rejection directed to absence of access should be removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant provides assurance, the examiner should remove the rejection; otherwise the rejection will be repeated until satisfied. Nonresponsive replies may result in abandonment; final rejections follow 37 CFR 1.116 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application in condition for allowance except for deposit — amendment after deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: After making the deposit, information regarding the deposit (depository name/address, accession number, date) to be added to the specification must be added by filing an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312, and such amendment must be filed before or with payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must make deposits early enough that the accession number is received with sufficient time to file the required amendment before paying the issue fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing XML requirement (37 CFR 1.831 and WIPO ST.26) for applications filed on/after July 1, 2022
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications disclosing one or more nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences by enumeration of residues must contain, as a separate part of the disclosure, a computer-readable Sequence Listing in XML format (a 'Sequence Listing XML') that conforms to the requirements of 37 CFR 1.831–1.834 and WIPO Standard ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Sequence Listing XML is a separate part of the specification and can be prepared in a single ST.26-compliant format suitable for use in all WIPO member state IPOs; ST.26 is incorporated by reference via 37 CFR 1.839.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing is part of the disclosure and may serve as application part
rubrics_metrics.description: For U.S. applications the sequence listing content is considered part of the disclosure of the invention; for international applications, sequences in the sequence listing are considered an application part if present on the filing date without incorporation by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sequence listing does not have to be duplicated elsewhere in the application for U.S. filings; however, the listing's content is part of the disclosure and relevant to 35 U.S.C. 112 considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'enumeration of its residues' (what counts as sequence disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Enumeration of its residues' means disclosure of a nucleotide or amino acid sequence by listing, in order, each residue of the sequence, where residues are represented as defined in WIPO ST.26 (either individual residue names/abbreviations/symbols or shorthand formulas like His6Gln).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See WIPO ST.26 examples and Guidance (Annex VI) for acceptable representations and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which sequences must be included or excluded from Sequence Listing XML (length thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Sequence Listing XML' must include nucleotide sequences that are unbranched or linear regions of a branched sequence of 10 or more specifically defined nucleotides, and amino acid sequences that are unbranched or linear regions of 4 or more specifically defined amino acids. Sequences with fewer than 10 nucleotides or fewer than 4 amino acids must be excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.831(j) and MPEP §§ 2412.03(d),(e) for definitions of nucleotide, modified nucleotide, and 'specifically defined'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'specifically defined' and allowed symbols (nucleotide and amino acid symbol tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Specifically defined' means any amino acid or nucleotide other than those represented by the symbol 'X' (amino acids) or 'n' (nucleotides) as defined in paragraph 3(k) of WIPO ST.26. WIPO ST.26 Annex I Tables list allowed nucleotide and amino acid symbols (e.g., a,c,g,t,m,r,w,s,y,k,v,h,d,b,n; A,R,N,D,C,Q… etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the symbol tables reproduced from ST.26 (MPEP § 2412.03) to determine whether residues are 'specifically defined'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and disclosure rules for modified amino acids
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified amino acids should be represented in the sequence as the corresponding unmodified amino acids where possible. Any modified amino acid that cannot be represented by a symbol in Table 3 must be represented by 'X' and further described in a feature table (feature keys such as CARBOHYD, LIPID with qualifier 'note' or MOD_RES/SITE with 'note').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The qualifier 'note' value must be an abbreviation from Table 4 or the full unabbreviated name of the modified amino acid; these abbreviations or full names must not be used inside the sequence itself. See MPEP § 2413.01(g) for feature table guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and representation of nucleotides and modified nucleotides
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Nucleotide' includes any nucleotide, nucleotide analog, or modified nucleotide as defined in WIPO ST.26 paragraphs 3(f) and 3(g). Modified nucleotides include nucleotides other than the standard monophosphates and may have various backbone moieties (e.g., PNA, glycol, morpholino, TNA) and still be considered nucleotides if they mimic natural base arrangements and can base-pair, or may represent AP/abasic sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult WIPO ST.26 and MPEP § 2412.03(e) for detailed backbone moiety examples and representation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sequence identifiers (SEQ ID NO:) when referencing sequences in description/claims/drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the description or claims discuss a sequence set forth in the Sequence Listing XML, reference must be made to the sequence by use of the sequence identifier (preceded by 'SEQ ID NO:' or the like) in the text of the description or claims. For sequences in drawings, reference must be made by sequence identifier either in the drawing or in the Brief Description of the Drawings where correlation is clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence identifiers in the disclosure must correspond to those in the Sequence Listing XML. Identifiers permit shorthand references (e.g., 'residues 14 to 243 of SEQ ID NO:23') and do not alter 35 U.S.C. 112 requirements; they merely permit discussion and claiming without re-enumerating the sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference and availability of WIPO ST.26 (37 CFR 1.839)
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO Standard ST.26 (ST.26: Recommended Standard for the Presentation of Nucleotide and Amino Acid Sequence Listings Using XML, version 1.6) is incorporated by reference into the USPTO regulations for §§ 1.831–1.834 via 37 CFR 1.839, and is available for inspection at the USPTO and NARA and from WIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the ST.26 standard and the USPTO Sequence Listing Resource Center for formatting and technical details (links provided in MPEP § 2412).
